t: #3682 Minimum Index Sum of Common Elements
o: Find the minimum i + j over pairs with nums1[i] == nums2[j]. Precompute the first occurrence index of each value in nums1, then scan nums2 combining with those indices; keep the minimum sum. Values fit in a hash map easily at n <= 1e5.
k: Only the first occurrence of each value in nums1 matters for minimizing i + j.
One hash map plus one linear scan solves it in O(n).

a.n: Approach 1: Hash map of first occurrences
a.i: Store value -> smallest index in nums1. For each j in nums2, if the value exists, candidate = firstIndex + j; answer is the minimum candidate or -1.
s: Build map value -> first index in nums1.
Scan nums2; for hits, relax the answer with index + j.
a.t: O(n) — two linear passes with hash-map operations.

w: Note the method name here is the LeetCode signature for this problem (minimumSum despite the 'index sum' phrasing). Negative values are fine since we hash rather than bucket. Follow-up: return all common elements achieving the minimum, or handle unequal lengths (same solution).
